title: Pnar Laho Dance Song (Chyiem Chui-Chui)
cultural_context: The traditional dance song of the Pnar people of Jowai and the Jaintia Hills. During the Laho dance festival, a maiden dances between two male partners with linked arms, moving gracefully in rhythm without drums, accompanied solely by the traditional bamboo flute (shyngwiang) and vocal rhyming chants marked by the cheerful refrain 'Chui-chui, chyiem chui-chui'.
lyrics_khasi:
Chyiem chui-chui, chyiem chui-chui!
Ia kynjoh kti ban shad ha madan;
Ka kynthei hapdeng, ki shynrang harud,
Ha ka sur Laho ba sawa thiang!

U shyngwiang u pyrsad ha ki lum Jowai,
Ki khun ka Ri Jaintia ki la kmen;
Khlem ksing khlem nakra ngi shad da ka sur,
Ka akor ba bha ngin pynneh ha tnum!

Chyiem chui-chui, ia kynjoh ban kmen,
Ka nam u Pnar kan neh ha pyrthei!
lyrics_english:
Chyiem chui-chui, chyiem chui-chui!
Link hands together to dance upon the field;
The maiden in the center, the young men on either flank,
Stepping to the sweet melodious cadence of Laho!

The bamboo shyngwiang flute breathes upon the hills of Jowai,
The sons and daughters of Jaintia rejoice in unity;
Without heavy drums or kettle-drums we dance to human melody,
Preserving our honorable ancestral traditions forever!

Chyiem chui-chui, step together in high delight,
The honorable name of the Pnar shall endure across the earth!

stanzas.title: Ka Shad Laho ha Madan (The Laho Dance)
stanzas.khasi:
Chyiem chui-chui, chyiem chui-chui!
Ia kynjoh kti ban shad ha madan;
Ka kynthei hapdeng, ki shynrang harud,
Ha ka sur Laho ba sawa thiang!
stanzas.english: Chyiem chui-chui! Join hands to dance upon the grass; maiden in the middle, men at her sides, moving to sweet Laho melodies!

stanzas.title: U Shyngwiang ha Jowai (Flute of Jowai)
stanzas.khasi:
U shyngwiang u pyrsad ha ki lum Jowai,
Ki khun ka Ri Jaintia ki la kmen;
Khlem ksing khlem nakra ngi shad da ka sur,
Ka akor ba bha ngin pynneh ha tnum!
stanzas.english: The bamboo flute blows over Jowai hills, Jaintia youth rejoice; without heavy drums we dance to sweet singing, honoring ancestral grace!

vocabulary.chyiem chui-chui: Traditional rhythmic refrain chanted during Pnar Laho folk dances
vocabulary.laho: The graceful festival dance of the Pnar people of Jowai and Jaintia Hills
vocabulary.shyngwiang: Traditional Pnar transverse bamboo flute with delicate ethereal tone
vocabulary.kynjoh kti: To link arms or clasp hands in synchronized communal dancing line
